name: Corinne "Cory" Vance
equipment: Snub-nose .38 revolver (5 rounds), carried in her handbag since a stalker in 2019
KHCF 1340 AM station keys, including the transmitter room
Ferry Days emcee lanyard and a wireless microphone with a dead battery
features: Specialist (Human (Specialist): +2 Charisma, +1 Wisdom, extra skill proficiency in Performance)
Silver Tongue (expertise in Persuasion and Insight: double proficiency bonus, +4 instead of +2)
Rally (bonus action: an ally who can hear her gains 1d6 + 3 temporary hit points and may end being frightened or Shaken; 3 uses per long rest)
On the Air (Journalist feature: everyone in Haskett County knows her voice from the KHCF morning show, and people who would not talk to a stranger will talk to her)

personality.traits: I narrate under pressure — out loud, like it's the morning show — and it calms everyone down, including me. I remember everybody's name, their kids' names and what they told me last time.
personality.ideals: People have a right to know what is happening to them. Silence is how the worst things get done.
personality.bonds: KHCF. Twenty-two years of mornings. If there is anybody left out there with a radio, they should hear a voice they know.
personality.flaws: I have been the most popular person in every room in this county for twenty years and I am not good at being disliked. I tell people what they want to hear more often than I should.

appearance: Forty-six, petite, with a sleek silver bob, red reading glasses on a beaded chain and a big warm laugh. Was emceeing Ferry Days from the flatbed stage in a denim jacket, a sundress and cowboy boots, and is still wearing all three. Her voice is a rich, warm alto that people recognise before they see her.
backstory: Corinne Vance has hosted 'Mornings with Cory' on KHCF 1340 AM since she was twenty-four: farm prices, school closings, the obituaries, the high-school football scores, and an hour every Friday of call-in gossip that most of the county pretends not to listen to. She has interviewed three governors, every sheriff since 2004 and the woman who grew the largest pumpkin in Missouri. She was on the flatbed stage at Ferry Days announcing the dunk-tank schedule when the screaming started, and she kept talking into the microphone — calmly telling people which way to run — until the generator was shot out. Several people are alive because of that, and she does not know which ones.
